items.description: after the up migration, a seeded conforming row (inventory_code "A12-B7-S001") has batch_number = "B7" and serial_number = "S001" and remains retrievable with its quantity and location intact (read back via the repository on the shared branch UP state)

on an isolated ephemeral branch (@pytest.mark.migration), seeding representative pre-migration stock rows (idempotent uuid-suffixed SKUs) then running the up migration leaves every seeded row present and retrievable with its quantity, sku and location intact, regardless of whether its code parsed

after the up migration, a seeded nonconforming row (inventory_code "X-1" or bare "c") has batch_number and serial_number left NULL rather than guessed or defaulted, and the row still survives and is retrievable (shared branch UP state)

batch_number and serial_number carry no NOT NULL constraint: inserting a stock row with both columns NULL against the branch DB succeeds (real DB session, shared branch UP state), proving the migration added them NULLABLE per PI3

after the up migration on a seeded row whose inventory_code leading segment differs from its location column, the location column is unchanged and still canonical; the code's leading segment did not overwrite location (shared branch UP state)

the UNIQUE(sku, location) constraint from F1 survives this migration: inserting two rows with the same (sku, location) against the branch DB raises an IntegrityError, confirming the composite key was neither dropped nor duplicated (real DB session, shared branch UP state)

after the up migration the stock_records table no longer exposes a combined inventory_code column and batch_number + serial_number are present as first-class columns (column introspection via the repository on the shared branch UP state)

the integrity probe, run over only this test's own seeded mix of conforming and nonconforming rows (filtered by the test's own SKUs), returns exactly the count of that seeded set's nonconforming rows; the assertion is scoped to the test's own rows, never an absolute whole-table total (shared branch UP state)

on an isolated ephemeral branch (@pytest.mark.migration), applying up-then-down (alembic downgrade -1) re-adds inventory_code and reconstructs it for conforming rows as location + '-' + batch_number + '-' + serial_number; the schema and conforming rows round-trip (reconstruction is lossy only for nonconforming rows left NULL); never downgrade the shared verify branch
